summary: First QA review of game-0001. Core loop mechanics (30 s countdown, expiry rewind with respawn, layered ghost replays that hold plates/doors/block lasers, timeline bar, reset, level-complete summary, four-chapter/six-level menus, deterministic replays) are established by current capture, replay and pixel evidence. Delivery is blocked: no demo_outputs traces ship at all, no Kenney/OpenGameArt assets were copied (all art is generated), the ghost button-press prop is never instantiated, the rewind flash overlay never decays (frame 599 fully washed out), the level-select header renders literal 'Chapter %d', and several ordinary-play actions (jump airborne, ENTER interact, level-button entry, Reset button click) plus enemy distraction and coordination-gating remain untested. Verdict: not ready.
instruction_audit: The instruction is internally coherent: the 20 s trace cap vs the 30 s loop is reconciled by permitted deterministic named scenarios (not a conflict), and pause/ESCAPE is a Designer assumption, not an instruction requirement, so it must not become a new acceptance criterion. Two audit findings: (1) the instruction mandates browsing and copying from the read-only library mounts, but gives no fallback if a mount is unavailable; the art manifest (untrusted) claims mounts were unavailable and substituted generated art, so host confirmation of mount availability is an unresolved instruction-omission risk kept visible as QA-ASSET-LIB. (2) 'The ghost physically interacts with the world: it presses buttons' is an explicit instruction verb with no Designer-level omission; its absence is an implementation gap (QA-DEV-BUTTONS), not a design conflict. No acceptance criterion was found to contradict or overstate the instruction, so no design_conflict verdicts are issued.

readiness_rationale: Not ready: host gate packaged_traces_replayed is false and the project ships zero demo_outputs traces (blocker QA-PACKAGE-001); library asset sourcing is absent (QA-ASSET-LIB); the ghost button-press verb is unimplemented (QA-DEV-BUTTONS); a major visual defect leaves the screen washed out after every rewind (QA-VIS-FLASH); and multiple core behaviors (jump, interact, enemy distraction, coordination gating, level-button entry) remain untested. Current build passes and core loop/ghost/replay mechanics are genuinely evidenced, but delivery readiness requires all requirements verified, packaged traces with fresh replays, final art, and no open major/blocker issues.
limitations: Visual review was limited to the eight supplied screenshot pixels; unseen frames and scenes are not visually verified.
The 600-frame (20 s) capture cap prevents observing a full ordinary 30 s loop expiry or four player-stacked loops without named scenarios.
result_state and loop_rewrite_imminent are prepared scenarios; they demonstrate rules and transitions but not ordinary player-earned completion.
Player interpretations and Developer MCP diagnostics were treated as leads only, never as acceptance evidence.
Static passes rely on inspected current source files plus build-0001 provenance; they do not establish runtime behavior beyond the cited sessions.
Mount availability for /workspace/assets/library and library-oga could not be independently confirmed from this payload.
